papers.title: Who Has the Ball?
papers.description_html:
Modern collaboration systems successfully model many aspects of cooperative work, including projects, documents, conversations, tasks, ownership, permissions, workflows, and automation. Yet they routinely fail to answer one of the simplest operational questions:

Who has the ball?

This question is deceptively fundamental. It does not ask who owns a project, who is accountable for an outcome, who was originally assigned a task, or who possesses authority over a resource. Rather, it asks who currently holds the live responsibility, context, and expectation to advance a particular unit of work.

Existing collaboration systems approximate this concept through fragmented mechanisms such as assignees, ownership fields, Kanban cards, RACI matrices, incident handoffs, or chain-of-custody procedures. However, these mechanisms typically model planning, accountability, or artifact provenance rather than the current possession of responsibility-bearing work.

This paper proposes Work Custody as a first-class primitive of collaboration. Work Custody is a temporally bounded constitutional relation describing which participant or execution role presently holds an accepted, scoped obligation to advance a work object, how custody is acquired and transferred, and how the collaboration system maintains shared queryable recognition among authorized participants. The record does not itself confer capability, authority, accountability, or moral or legal responsibility.

The proposed protocol grammar can be used across human-human, human-agent, and agent-agent collaboration, while participant type, capability, authority, accountability, and legal or moral responsibility remain distinct. It offers a candidate operational primitive for constitutional collaboration environments.

papers.title: A Formal Theory of Work Custody
papers.description_html:
This paper proposes Work Custody as a first-class collaboration relation identifying which eligible participant currently holds the bounded operational duty to advance a particular version and scope of a work object. Custody answers "who has the next move?" without collapsing ownership, assignment, authority, accountability, capability, or standing.

The model replaces an informal linear status list with a generation-bound state machine. Offers, acceptances, transfers, releases, revocations, expirations, completion, blockage, and recovery are typed transitions. A normal transfer is a handshake: the predecessor remains primary until the successor accepts and the transfer is promoted. Forced revocation or failure may create an explicit unassigned or recovery-required state; the system preserves accountability for the discontinuity rather than pretending custody never had a gap.

Custody is queryable only relative to exact work identity, version, scope, valid time, transaction time, jurisdiction, and authorization. Receipts bind declarations and observations but do not by themselves prove complete mediation or actual effect. Human and machine participants may share transition syntax while differing in capability, persistence, consent, legal personality, and moral accountability.

The resulting specification supports agent orchestration, cold-boot continuity, governed project memory, and cross-node handoff. It remains a candidate architecture: implementation conformance, organizational benefit, complexity reduction, and comparative performance require exact configurations and empirical evidence.

papers.title: Exigence and the Cognitive Kernel
papers.description_html:
Computational systems routinely model tasks, priorities, deadlines, permissions, attention, and action, but they rarely possess a unified account of why a particular state presently calls for transition. This paper introduces Exigence as a first-class computational primitive: the graph-derived condition by which an object, process, agent, institution, or environment presently calls for some admissible change. Exigence is neither priority nor urgency. Priority is declared ordering; urgency concerns time sensitivity; Exigence arises from the live relationship between state, dependency, consequence, opportunity, authority, capability, care, safety, and constraint.

The paper situates Exigence within a broader Cognitive Kernel, or CogK, that separates observation, salience, epistemic interpretation, Exigence, standing, attention, custody, sufficiency, policy, authorization, execution, receipt, and outcome. These elements are treated not as interchangeable stages but as distinct projections over shared governed reality. The separation allows systems to distinguish what is observed from what is believed, what matters from what may be done, and what may be done from what actually occurred.

The resulting architecture supports lawful refusal, receipt-before-effect, context compilation, agent orchestration, institutional modeling, attention governance, household coordination, autonomous systems, games, simulated societies, and the progressive crystallization of expensive semantic reasoning into deterministic machinery. It also permits the modeling of pathological Exigence topologies such as fixation, suppression, inflation, avoidance, fragmentation, and over-propagation. These structures need not be used to diagnose humans. They can instead serve as integrity and execution-gate models for detecting recurrent computational trajectories that should be refused, escalated, reinterpreted, or repaired.

The central claim is that Exigence is a candidate connective layer between a passive world model and governed transition. Its value depends on keeping an Exigence claim distinct from observation, salience, standing, attention, policy, authorization, effect, and outcome. The Cognitive Kernel thereby offers a general substrate for systems that must decide what currently matters, who holds the next move, what conditions are sufficient, what transitions are lawful, and when action must stop.

papers.title: Constraint-Bearing Composability
papers.description_html:
Constraint-Bearing Composability presents a diagnostic ontology for analyzing how components form valid, reusable, and governable wholes. Rather than treating composability as a binary property, the framework distinguishes aggregation, proposal, formation, compatibility, realization, retention, invariant preservation, component standing, recursive closure, and architectural admissibility.

The paper introduces constraint carriage as the allocation of responsibility for realizing and preserving designated invariants across observers, environments, component-intrinsic structures, interfaces, mediators, internal organization, architectures, and constitutional rules. Compositional claims are evaluated relative to a declared disturbance envelope, residual assumptions, evidence, failure conditions, and lifecycle state.

The framework separates four judgment layers that are often conflated: a relation may be proposed, a composite may form, the formed composite may or may not be valid, and a governing regime may or may not admit reliance upon it. Standing—the justified eligibility of an object to be treated as a bounded component for a declared purpose—is modeled as a distinct, evidence-dependent status.

A configuration-level account explains why individually valid components and locally compatible relations may still produce a globally inadmissible architecture through dependency cycles, authority amplification, privacy leakage, semantic contradiction, resource exhaustion, correlated failure, or hidden environmental assumptions. Worked profiles involving interlocking bricks, evidence modules, and linked datasets demonstrate both successful and failing compositions.

The framework complements hierarchy theory, modularity, interface theory, contract-based design, architectural mismatch analysis, and compositional reasoning. It is intended as a cross-domain vocabulary and diagnostic instrument for physical, computational, epistemic, institutional, and economic systems, while leaving domain-specific proof, testing, measurement, certification, and governance to appropriate specialized methods.

papers.title: Constitutional Synchronization
papers.description_html:
Software systems rarely possess one authoritative representation of themselves. They exist simultaneously as requirements, semantic models, schemas, transition rules, source code, binaries, runtime processes, tests, receipts, authority records, documentation, and user interfaces. These representations may begin in agreement and later diverge independently. An application can execute successfully while running unadmitted bytes, preserving obsolete semantics, relying upon stale evidence, exercising revoked authority, or presenting users with a projection that no longer corresponds to constitutional state.

This paper introduces constitutional synchronization, a domain-neutral framework for maintaining governed correspondence among the identity, meaning, lawful transitions, executable realizations, observed behavior, evidence, authority, history, dependencies, and public projections of a system. Constitutional synchronization does not collapse specification into implementation. It preserves their distinction while making the path between them explicit, identity-bearing, witnessed, and enforceable.

A system is constitutionally synchronized for a declared purpose when its current realization can be shown to correspond to its admitted model and transition law; its execution is adequately witnessed; its evidence supports its current standing; its authority remains valid; its dependencies and historical lineage are current; and its external projections faithfully expose the relevant constitutional state. The framework distinguishes synchronization from equality, divergence from insufficient evidence, local synchronization from configuration-level synchronization, and resynchronization from ordinary mutation.

The paper develops a formal model, a taxonomy of desynchronization, a system of constitutional courts, a synchronization-state vocabulary, and a governed resynchronization process. It further examines executable specification, content-addressed intake, user-interface projection, recursive self-hosting, and constitutionally bounded self-improvement. The central claim is that the traditional gulf between specification and implementation is not overcome by eliminating either side, but by maintaining enforceable correspondence across every identity-bearing layer through which meaning becomes effect.

papers.title: A Constitution for the Context Window
papers.description_html:
Large language models do not encounter users, projects, institutions, or environments directly. Each provider invocation presents the model with a bounded construction assembled from governing policy, retrieved evidence, runtime observations, persistent memory, tools and capability descriptions, selected history, the current user request, and vendor or base-system instruction.

These source classes form PROMTHUS:

Policy, Retrieval, Observations, Memory, Tools, History, User request, System instruction.

PROMTHUS is an inventory, not an authority hierarchy or serialization order. Its sequence serves a mnemonic and Promethean construction; it does not imply that Policy is universally supreme or that later classes possess lower standing. PROMTHUS names the principal materials from which an invocation context is compiled.

To promthe an invocation is to subject those materials to constitutional context compilation: governed discovery, authentication, semantic finding, independently derived consequence analysis, contest, adjudication, authorized transformation, budget closure, provider realization, effect authorization, and evidentiary sealing.

This paper proposes constitutional context compilation as a typed authorization, adjudication, and transformation layer between context sources and inference. The compiler governs what may count as context, what may govern inference, what may be disclosed, how admitted context may be transformed, what may cross a provider boundary, which consequences may follow, and what must remain auditable afterward.

The architecture defines the minimum contract required of a Constitutional Kernel capable of governing context compilation. Such a kernel must provide an explicit and non-extensible bootstrap basis, identity-bearing root law, governed discovery obligations, authorized amendment, court jurisdiction, non-self-ratification, typed judgment, structurally triggered contest, review and appeal, refusal semantics, independent effect authorization, and witness.

The paper distinguishes a presupposed Grundnorm Basis from a positive, executable Root Constitution written in Deterministic Semantic Compiler (DSC) form. DSC coding means that law is expressed as explicit, canonically serializable, content-identified rules that execute deterministically over admitted structured predicates, rather than as prose whose application depends on interpretation at the moment of use. The Grundnorm Basis identifies the genesis custody and initial standing that any finite constitutional order must presuppose. It is fixed at genesis and cannot later be enlarged by declaration. The Root Constitution makes operational successor law deterministic over admitted structured predicates, inspectable, content-identified, testable, auditable, and mutable only through authorized amendment.

Context-specific law derives from that root. Discovery profiles, calibration profiles, conflict-detection profiles, independence profiles, domain canonicalization profiles, consequence tiers, court procedures, provider-adapter contracts, and effect boundaries all receive standing from law outside the discretion they constrain. Any profile whose declarations bound the scope of scrutiny must be identity-bearing, evidence-class-typed, and adjudicated before use.

Identity itself is layered to avoid a bootstrap circularity. A primitive, exclusion-free Constitutional Canonical Form (CCaF), bound into the genesis recognition machinery, identifies constitutional objects; adjudicated domain profiles govern application material. Every identity is permanently typed by the layer under which it was computed, and relations across layers are typed correspondences rather than collapsible equivalences.

Completeness of governance is made checkable rather than asserted. A discretion census over the declared schema and transition registry enumerates every mechanism able to affect identity, authority, admission, scope, scrutiny, conflict detection, transformation, realization, effect permission, or evidentiary claims, and each censused locus must bind to an audit row or a proven reduction to one.

Classifiers do not become lawmakers; their outputs become receipted findings subject to calibration, conservative consequence computation, independent contest, judicial review, appeal, and refusal. The context compiler executes admitted judgments. The Context Intermediate Representation is the identity-bearing product of that governed process, not its source of authority.

The architecture distinguishes six principal failures: context loss, containment loss, authority loss, representation loss, realization loss, and receipt loss. It defines three layers of context identity over two canonicalization layers, strict partial-order precedence, inter-court conflict law, scrutiny-profile adjudication, cross-layer correspondence, governing projections, delegation contracts, autonomous-loop review, availability protections against stay flooding, privacy-preserving receipts, two-phase budget closure, staged conformance, and measurable governance cost.

Its general constitutional proposition is:

Every mechanism that determines whether another mechanism is scrutinized must itself be governed by authority external to the discretion it constrains.

The paper audits the architecture against that proposition by enumerating its discretionary loci, the power held at each locus, the external governor, the evidentiary record, and the failure emitted when governance is absent. The discretion census supplies the enumeration procedure, so the audit's completeness claim rests on a declared schema rather than on architectural omniscience.

The architecture does not prove truth, model understanding, obedience, classifier completeness, contest independence beyond available evidence, profile completeness beyond available evidence, or remote-provider honesty. This paper specifies a narrower conditional assurance claim: a conforming realization may establish, relative to its declared capability surface and evidence, that context was assembled under explicit machine-governance rules, adjudicated through authorized procedures, realized according to an admitted adapter contract, and bound to evidence sufficient for later inspection. The paper itself is a proposal and proof-obligation map; it supplies no implementation-conformance verdict.

A constitutional context layer could unify memory, retrieval, personalization, policy, capability exposure, delegation, and long-running automation within one systems discipline. It would also make durable computational agency portable across replaceable inference providers---where the user or another legitimate custodian actually holds the registry, amendment authority, and receipts on which such portability depends.

papers.title: From Content-Addressed Storage to Governed Semantic Project Lineage
papers.description_html:
This paper examines whether the proposed Semantic Project Lineage System represents a genuinely new computing architecture or primarily recombines established mechanisms.

The proposed system is a local-first, content-addressed, transtemporal substrate for storing, reconstructing, governing, and navigating evolving digital projects. It represents projects through exact content objects, persistent file-state lineages, version-scoped path maps, provenance and authority relationships, and reconstructible external projections such as ZIP archives and working directories.

The system is designed in particular for human--AI project workflows. An AI agent may repeatedly emit a complete project artifact under the same visible filename. Before that artifact replaces the prior visible version, the substrate independently verifies continuity, identifies every predecessor-file disposition, refuses unexplained losses, commits newly admitted content, and preserves exact reconstruction of prior states.

The review finds substantial prior art for nearly every primitive involved:

  • content-addressed immutable storage;
  • global chunk deduplication;
  • snapshot-based version control;
  • mutable objects formed from immutable claims;
  • semantic filesystem indexing;
  • data provenance;
  • reproducible derivation;
  • versioned data repositories;
  • staged agent filesystem mutation;
  • Git-like agent memory and rollback.

However, the reviewed systems do not appear to combine these mechanisms into the same authority model and operating workflow.

The strongest differentiation is not a new hashing, chunking, graph, or delta algorithm. It is an architectural unification:

The ordinary filesystem, project archive, and agent workspace become projections of a governed semantic-temporal graph whose authoritative state includes exact content, file ancestry, project membership, provenance, authority, causality, and reconstructible external representations.

The paper therefore concludes that the proposed system is best characterized as a plausibly novel systems synthesis built from established primitives. Its strongest research contribution would be a governed correspondence model connecting exact storage, semantic project history, safe agent publication, and ordinary filesystem usability. The novelty claim remains review-bounded: it describes the comparison set represented in this draft, not universal priority, patentability, or the absence of other systems. The paper also supplies a formal object model and proof obligations so that the synthesis can be evaluated as more than a feature list.

papers.title: Legitimacy Without Self-Ratification
papers.description_html:
What makes a state transition legitimate when the system performing the transition can also modify the rules, evidence, memories, trust anchors, or verification procedures by which that transition will later be judged?

This paper argues that reflexive computational systems face a problem of legitimacy distinct from correctness, security, integrity, or epistemic warrant. A transition may produce a correct result and nevertheless be unauthorized. It may be well-supported by evidence while lacking authority. It may preserve data integrity while changing the conditions under which integrity itself is defined. The central failure mode is self-ratification: the subject whose standing is in question supplies the decisive warrant by which that standing is conferred.

We develop a substrate-independent account of this problem and a computational architecture for addressing it. For a protected reflexive transition, there must exist no supporting evidence set that is sufficient to confer decisive standing and lies entirely under the unilateral control of the subject whose standing is being adjudicated. We formalize this principle using antecedent authorization, threat-model-relative control, typed provenance, evidence ablation, standing ceilings, defeaters, constitutional epochs, non-retroactivity, governed amendment, congruence between declared and executable law, and replayable transition receipts. We show that anti-self-ratification is not sufficient in isolation: its guarantee is constitutionally closed only when the rules defining evidence, standing, amendment, and verification are themselves governed by antecedent law.

The argument is interdisciplinary but not reductionist. Epistemic warrant, due process, legal validity, political legitimacy, constitutionalism, integrity, authorization logic, reference monitors, proof-carrying code, supply-chain provenance, transparency logs, Byzantine consensus, corrigibility, and constitutional AI are not synonyms. Rather, they exhibit a recurrent formal concern: power must not become sufficient evidence of its own rightful exercise. Their relation resembles Aristotelian focal meaning, or pros hen predication: distinct concepts retain distinct objects and failure conditions while exhibiting consilience around a shared semantic center.

The source manuscript reports a reference implementation in which anti-self-ratification is an explicit, load-bearing invariant. Its reported release process distinguishes self-description from external ratification; its verifier boundary rejects self-certification as sufficient evidence of verifier trustworthiness; its executor is reported to prohibit promotion of solely executor-authored evidence to the highest standing class; and its history is reported to support defeasible standing without erasure. A naturally occurring defect is also reported to have exposed the importance of evidence beyond the system's own observation boundary. This candidate preserves those claims as author-reported implementation evidence. Replayability, independence, authority, and epistemic strength remain separate, and no report is upgraded without its exact artifact and custody chain.

The paper also treats failures of the constitutional cure. A governance mechanism can fail by admitting what should be forbidden, but also by obstructing what its own law purports to permit. We therefore introduce governed liveness and governance proportionality, together with a two-lane architecture in which low-standing exploration remains cheap while high-standing acceptance receives full certification.

The broader thesis is that legitimacy is not essentially political and constitutionalism is not merely metaphorical. Wherever a subject can change consequential state while also influencing the grounds on which that change is accepted, a legitimacy problem appears. Constitutional computing names an architectural response: power over state is subordinated to prior, inspectable, amendable, and independently checkable rules governing the provenance of authority.

The present candidate does not infer empirical results from the protocol. The source reports execution of its conformance and mutation suite and independent replay of principal courts, but this integration pass did not recover the exact archives, court packages, command transcripts, or independently retained outputs required to re-establish those claims. Appendix C therefore preserves the reports while withholding independent-verification standing. The distinction is the theory functioning correctly.

papers.title: From CI/CD to ACG: From Tests to Courts in Agentic Software Development
papers.description_html:
Continuous integration and continuous delivery transformed software engineering by making builds, tests, packaging, and deployment checks part of the infrastructure of change rather than optional developer practices. Agentic coding changes the limiting problem. As software agents become capable of generating and modifying implementation faster than humans can directly review it, the central engineering bottleneck shifts from code production toward epistemic and constitutional control: determining what a change means, whether an implementation corresponds to its specification, whether available evidence establishes the claimed behavior, whether previous evidence remains applicable to the exact current subject, whether a transition is authorized, what concrete effect should occur, and what may truthfully be claimed afterward.

This paper introduces Ableman Constitutional Governance (ACG) as a software-development architecture in which a constitutionally significant subset of executable verification is promoted from tests into courts. Within the software domain considered here,

C_{\mathrm{software}} \subseteq V_{\mathrm{executable}},

where ordinary unit, integration, regression, determinism, packaging, performance, and recurrence tests remain part of the broader verification estate. Courts differ not because they cease to be executable verifications, but because selected predicates are bound to an exact subject, constitutional frame, proposition or obligation, evidence topology, jurisdiction, authority relationship, and typed disposition.

The paper develops a broader claim: the reasoning capability obtained from ACG does not arise from courts alone. It arises from combining constitutionally typed verification with constitutional synchronization, governed effects, and a richer representation of the system. Ableman's Razor, originally formulated as a typed grammar governing migration of claims among Specification, Configuration, and Implementation, is explicitly extended here as a representation lens for governed systems. The current integration resolves Configuration into Configuration Manifold 1 (CM1), the mandatory admissible manifold; Configuration Manifold 2 (CM2), the preferred admissible manifold under declared criteria; and IC, expanded interchangeably as Instance Constitution or Instance Configuration, the selected slice for a concrete system. IR, expanded interchangeably as Instance Realization or Implementation Realization, makes that selection concrete:

P\rightarrow S\rightarrow CM_1\rightarrow CM_2\rightarrow IC\rightarrow IR\rightarrow E\rightarrow R.

This extension is not attributed to the Razor's original jurisdiction. It is accepted only insofar as the added layers yield diagnostic, governance, selection, correspondence, evidence, or revision distinctions unavailable from a less differentiated representation without equivalent structure.

This representation connects to Dynatology, the study of possible continuation: which transitions are conceivable, specification-valid, admissible, reachable, viable, selected, authorized, realized, observed, and established from a particular state. ACG supplies courts that adjudicate relationships and transitions among these projections.

The architecture also extends governance into consequential execution through constitutional effect interposition. Application logic may continue to propose familiar semantic operations while a governed effect boundary determines the admissible realization under the current Instance Constitution. The requested operation, admitted realization, and actual observed effect are therefore distinct:

O_r \rightarrow R_a \rightarrow E_a.

A governed boundary may preserve, negate, constrain, transform, defer, simulate, sandbox, or substitute a proposed effect. This is not claimed to be novel merely as interception or mutation: reference monitors, capability systems, admission controllers, aspect-oriented programming, and effect handlers provide important precedents. The distinguishing concern is the integration of effect mediation with exact-subject binding, constitutional selection, evidentiary correspondence, typed dispositions, receipts, lineage, and standing.

Because governed effects cross explicit semantic boundaries, those same boundaries become causal observation points. Receipts can record what operation was proposed, what realization was admitted, what executor action occurred, and what post-effect evidence followed. Governance, behavioral adaptation, and debugging can therefore share one effect topology.

Documentation is similarly repositioned. Rather than remaining an independently authored and perpetually drifting artifact, documentation, glossaries, implementation codices, agent-orientation surfaces, capability references, operator explanations, and configuration views become deterministic, zero-authority projections of the retained semantic model. Projection fidelity does not itself establish realization fidelity; correspondence must be independently witnessed and adjudicated.

The paper defines a reasoning-capability gain operationally as a representational extension that, while holding the underlying observed system state fixed, enables derivation of a decision-relevant distinction, contradiction, obligation, or admissible-action restriction that the baseline representation cannot express or derive without introducing equivalent additional structure. Several development episodes illustrate this pattern: environmental extraction safety conflicted with realization fidelity; artifact reuse was separated from effectful materialization; source changes invalidated stale verification evidence; and historical verifiers were made to testify to their own supersession rather than masquerade as current authority.

The resulting software project is no longer modeled merely as source code plus tests and documentation. It becomes a constitutionally synchronized semantic and effect state containing specification, configuration possibilities, instance commitments, implementation bindings, evidence, courts, authority, effects, receipts, lineage, standing, and deterministic projections. ACG therefore suggests a progression from continuous integration toward continuous constitutionalization: not a replacement for CI/CD, but an enlargement in which verification, correspondence, adjudication, effect governance, and explanation become machine-addressable parts of the development process.

papers.title: The Locus of Meaning
papers.description_html:
Where does meaning exist? Two recurrent answers place it primarily in the world or primarily in the interpreting mind. The first treats meaning as an intrinsic or discoverable property of objects. The second treats meaning as a projection, representation, or construction of a perceiving subject. This paper argues that both answers misidentify the semantic locus. Meaning is constituted at the location of binding: the structured relation through which objects, signs, interpreters, contexts, histories, practices, distinctions, and consequences become mutually determining. Objects and minds can constrain, preserve, activate, and transform meaning, but neither is its exclusive container.

This thesis is formulated as the Semantic Binding Principle:

papers.title: A Cognitive ABI for Capability-Centered Computing
papers.description_html:
A capability should not be identified with the implementation that happens to realize it. This paper develops a cognitive ABI: a semantic contract boundary through which cognitive operations are composed, qualified, authorized, realized, and evaluated independently of a particular human, model, program, or system backend. Hybrid Semantic Compiler (HSC) theory supplies the distinction between Fuzzy Semantic Compiler (FSC) operation without established deterministic semantic closure and Deterministic Semantic Compiler (DSC) operation within a declared closure regime. The Cognitive Kernel (CogK) situates work through observation, epistemic position, Exigence, attention, custody, and sufficiency. The Three Hash Rule supplies independent commitments to state, admissibility, and meaning, with optional locality and separate receipt binding.

The ABI provides contracts both for work CogK proposes and for operations implementing CogK itself, without assigning CogK execution authority. Typed semantic residue preserves unresolved obligations and connects them to responsibility-bearing work. An evidence-carrying Workflow IR spans cognitive operations and system effects while distinguishing formal proof, deterministic checking, empirical qualification, and attested observation.

An author-verified vertical slice combines evidence custody binding, Action IR correspondence checking, deterministic fault evaluation, a bounded CGSOS system test under a one-shot warrant, and residue separation. It performs four DSC cognitive operations and one governed system effect, with zero model calls, network calls, or production changes. Focused tests and 105 bounded qualification trials support cross-plane feasibility. Genuine FSC residue discharge, the integrated CogK work-custody cycle, independent reproduction, and public artifact release remain outstanding. This architecture-and-artifact account makes meaning, competence, authority, effects, unresolved work, and evidence independently inspectable across changing realizations.

papers.title: The Locus of Qualia
papers.description_html:
What would it mean to specify the taste of mint mathematically? This paper proposes a contextual binding event as the explanatory unit for qualitative specificity: an organized occurrence in which sensory differentiation, bodily state, temporal history, attention, and other relevant constraints jointly determine a particular experiential character. The proposal extends the Semantic Binding Principle and its distinctions among identity, support, constitution, and realization. It does not follow deductively from that semantic framework. The qualitative event, its hypothesized constitutive organization, its physical realization, and the observations used to investigate it remain separately typed.

Mint provides a worked domain: weak and strong mint, peppermint and spearmint, fresh and dried preparations, decay-associated qualities, and evolving aftertaste. These form candidate regions and trajectories in a context-indexed experiential atlas, not predetermined coordinates in a universal Euclidean space. Typed dimensional distinction, statistical independence, geometric orthogonality, and causal selectivity are distinguished. Experiential-content coordinates are also separated from the Ableman Consciousness Ontology's binding-regime axes, Semantic Manifold Competence's operational capacities, and the epistemic properties of a research account.

A source-integrated architecture assigns different responsibilities to Locus, Global Term Key, Dynatology, Semantic Manifold Topology, Semantic Binding Quality, and the GMB/crystallization lineage as governance of the research account. Dynatology contributes explicit reachability; SMT contributes declared continuity auditing rather than an assumed geometry of experience; SBQ supplies candidate criteria for model integrity rather than a consciousness score. A new path-realization requirement shows why individually realizable projected transitions may form an unrealizable sequence when a chart identifies states with different continuations. A finite-path lifting criterion and a worked counterexample make this issue testable.

The contribution is a falsifiable research architecture, not an empirical demonstration of phenomenal constitution. Proposed studies compare typed, contextual, history-sensitive binding models with strong alternatives on held-out observations, interventions, and sequences. Limited mathematical results and two executable synthetic fixtures establish only properties of stipulated models. The strongest hypothesis remains that qualitative specificity is constituted by a particular realized binding organization; prediction, operational competence, governance admission, and causal correspondence do not individually establish that hypothesis.

Keywords: qualia; semantic binding; phenomenal structure; contextual realization; architectonics; experiential atlas; causal abstraction; psychophysics; representational geometry; mint; consciousness; identifiability.

papers.title: The Path Was Open
papers.description_html:
Machine action selection creates neither an automatic responsibility vacuum nor automatic human liability. This paper develops a boundary-accountability framework that separates selection autonomy from authority over effects; declared admissibility from operational reachability; and causal contribution, answerability, fault, and legal liability.

The technical core is the declared-effective boundary gap: modeled execution histories reachable under a configuration and threat model but excluded by the deployment's declared scope. A nonempty gap is evidence of a technical mismatch within the model. It does not establish probability, notice, duty, fault, intent, causation, or liability. An empty gap is equally bounded: it can enforce an illegitimate policy, omit real effect paths, or depend on unsound abstraction.

A conditional mediation proposition shows that prohibited modeled effects are excluded if every relevant effect passes through an accurate, non-bypassable gate whose allowed transitions preserve the declared safety property. The proposition is a specification theorem, not evidence that a deployment satisfies its premises. Real use requires exact configurations, concretization between abstract and physical effects, current authority, effect observation, bypass testing, custody, and independent verification.

The source reports an exhaustive 625-string finite illustration and says that a companion checker is supplied. No such program or result file was found in the authorized corpus. An independent AI reconstruction from the prose reproduced the reported counts, but that is conditional arithmetic validation rather than custody of the claimed author evidence. The source's 2026 incident and legal claims also remain author-supplied pending separately authorized primary-source verification.

This revision integrates the accountability framework with Authority Laundering Theory, constitutional enforcement, receipts, observability, work custody, Warrant by Structure, the universal GSM, and the realization funnel. It grants no factual, legal, safety, implementation, or publication standing.

papers.title: The Locus of Shared Experience
papers.description_html:
What does it mean for two people to share an experience without possessing identical experiences? This addendum extends the contextual experiential-binding proposal from the constitution of individual qualitative episodes to capability, mind attribution, experiential access, and intersubjective participation. Its central claim is that shared experience can be modeled as a higher-order, consequential binding among distinct participants and their encounters, preserving both warranted commonality and intelligible difference. The shared organization is not presumed to be a third phenomenal subject.

Six developments organize the argument. First, a cognitive capability is treated as a sustained achievement dependent on organization, constraints, resources, and conditions, rather than on complexity alone. Second, named faculties may compose overlapping formative capacities; the proposal does not posit a single dedicated detector or a specific evolutionary origin. Third, the realization of activity is separated from an observer's attribution of capability or experience. Fourth, experiential access is indexed by distinction, route, conditions, and occasion, avoiding a global ranking of consciousness from a local perceptual limitation. Fifth, semantic correspondence is formalized relative to a comparison contract and representational resolution: shared reference, category agreement, functional correspondence, and phenomenal identity remain different claims. Sixth, interpersonal understanding is distinguished from agreement. A more adequate account of another standpoint can preserve, clarify, or even reveal disagreement rather than eliminate it.

The formal development introduces partial semantic projections, resolution refinement, directional perspective bridges, standpoint-tagged difference accounts, and interaction-sensitive encounter records. Elementary propositions show that coarse equivalence need not imply finer equivalence, invariance need not imply truth, synchronized outputs need not imply reciprocal interaction, and predictive understanding need not increase with agreement. Proposed studies distinguish shared component reuse from generic task effects, attribution from target performance, alternative access from identical phenomenology, and contingent interaction from common exposure. The contribution is a source-grounded research architecture for making experiential commonality and difference answerable to inquiry, not a solution by definition to phenomenal identity or the existence of consciousness.

Keywords: shared experience; intersubjectivity; semantic binding; formative capability; realization shell; mind attribution; experiential access; co-projection; objectivity; perspective; mutual understanding; difference preservation.

papers.title: Admissibility Theory of Consciousness
papers.description_html:
Consciousness debates often promote familiar capacities of human minds into necessary conditions while leaving the underlying organization unspecified. This paper proposes the Admissibility Theory of Consciousness (ATC): admissibility--the distinction between eligible and excluded continuations--as a candidate structural kernel around which consciousness-relevant organization develops. The claim is not that every constrained process experiences, but that sensing, meaning-binding, persistence, reflexivity, and situated agency can be investigated as different organizations of constrained continuation. Drawing on Dynatology, ATC distinguishes conceivable transitions, admissible transitions, and realized trajectories; separates physical feasibility, epistemic warrant, and authorization; and distinguishes context-sensitive behavior from alteration of the governing relation. Five organizational regimes connect elementary constraint to situated sensitivity, persistence, reflexive representation, and authorized self-authorship without imposing a scalar consciousness ranking. The Ableman Consciousness Ontology supplies multidimensional description; Semantic Reactor Theory supplies a proposed, inspectable architecture of epistemic positioning, governance, execution, and feedback; Meaning--Inertia remains an optional physical hypothesis. The paper locates these proposals within process philosophy, cybernetics, organizational closure, enactivism, and contemporary consciousness research. Its principal obligation is empirical discrimination: specifying which organizations of admissibility explain evidence beyond generic descriptions of lawful dynamics. Phenomenality remains an explicit bridge problem, not a property established by definition.

Keywords: admissibility; constrained continuation; consciousness; reflexivity; meaning-binding; organizational closure; Dynatology; Semantic Reactor Theory.

papers.title: Model-First Legacy Migration
papers.description_html:
Legacy migration is usually framed as translation from one implementation to another. That framing leaves the most consequential uncertainty untouched: no one knows which observed behaviors are intended obligations, which are relied-upon accidents, which are defects, and which depend on an environment that the replacement does not reproduce. This paper develops a model-first alternative. A bounded behavioral model is extracted from exact source custody, static structure, observations, operational knowledge, policy, and downstream dependencies; it is then adjudicated before it may become normative. Candidate realizations are compared against both the model and the original system within declared envelopes, equivalence relations, observers, and claim ceilings.

The proposal does not solve general program equivalence or infer intention from behavior alone. It replaces an unaudited rewrite with a governed chain of explicit models, gaps, assumptions, tests, promotion decisions, rollback paths, and revision records. Its strongest capability is not automatic modernization. It is the conversion of hidden dependencies into inspectable and contestable migration obligations while preserving a disciplined refusal to claim beyond observed and justified evidence.

papers.title: Adversarial Alternation Under Human Governance
papers.description_html:
This paper reports a two-day case study in which two AI sessions alternated between builder and auditor roles while one human Governor retained scope, disposition, and ratification authority. The subject was a small verification and evidence-recovery system whose claims could be quarantined when a dependency failed and restored only after re-derivation and human ratification.

The case suggests a practical hardening loop: freeze the candidate, replay it cold, attack beyond packaged tests, reproduce every accepted finding before repair, convert each counterexample into a permanent regression, and prevent artifacts from conferring standing on themselves. The source reports that later builder errors were caught by earlier auditor tests and that the last ledger round had no findings under its probe set.

Those observations do not establish that alternation outperforms one careful agent. The sessions were role-separated but not shown to be epistemically independent; they were probably from the same model family. There was no baseline, the program was small, the author participated, probe sets changed, and findings were counted in inconsistent units. The frozen archives and full reports were not rerun in this review. The defensible contribution is therefore an evidence-bounded method specification and a set of hypotheses for controlled evaluation, not a causal effect claim.

papers.title: Sovereign Software
papers.description_html:
Possessing application source does not by itself establish control over the system that gives the application its behavior. Dependencies, build tools, runtimes, identity services, update channels, remote infrastructure, and hardware can retain powers that the nominal owner neither understands nor governs. This paper develops sovereign software as a relational and operational property: the ability of identified people or institutions to determine software meaning, constrain effects, inspect the grounds of assurance, and continue, repair, or replace required capabilities without ungranted control by an indispensable supplier. As a companion to Constitutional Computing: Evidence-Carrying Realization, Agentic Development, and the Economics of Structured Abundance, it presents sovereignty as the purpose that structured abundance can help make practical. It distinguishes legal freedom, source access, custody, security, and effective independence; develops a thirteen-axis custody profile and a claim-relative dependency-closure model; and treats reconstruction and provider-removal exercises as tests of meaningful exit. Constitutional contracts connect these requirements to independent evidence, locally governed adoption, and competing implementations. In universal-GSM terms, the paper follows sovereignty from possibility and specification through admissible and preferred configurations, a selected instance constitution/configuration, its instance/implementation realization, evidence, and revision. Agentic development and distributed publication are proposed as ways to turn opaque dependencies into bounded reliance relationships and, where feasible, replaceable realizations. Neither an attestation nor a complete inventory confers sovereignty by itself. The paper examines build bootstrap, information-flow limits, version sovereignty, closed-source adaptation, shared governance, and the risks of creating new gatekeepers around models or verification. An encrypted-messaging scenario and a falsifiable evaluation program specify how the approach could be investigated without claiming universal verification, zero residual trust, or a mature sovereign operating system.

Keywords: sovereign software; Constitutional Computing; software freedom; dependency custody; local-first software; reproducible builds; execution authority; effective exit; structured abundance.

papers.title: Modeling Stationary-to-Rotating Power Transfer with a Two-Machine EMRT
papers.description_html:
This paper develops a governed reference model for stationary-to-rotating electrical power transfer through a two-machine Electro-Mechanical Rotational Transformer (EMRT) arrangement. It specifies the topology, primitive set, invariants, machine and energy equations, control comparison, assigned simulation conditions, communication concepts, failure modes, evidence limits, and a bench-validation plan.

The current evidence is local software evidence. The reported results are bounded to the declared simulation configuration. No hardware trial, calibration certificate, safety approval, demonstrated efficiency advantage, priority claim, or novelty determination is asserted.

The EMRT technical brief and conceptual schematics are published as separately citable companion works.

papers.title: EMRT Technical Brief - Stationary Power for a Rotating Electrical Load
papers.description_html:
This technical brief provides a concise engineering orientation to a two-machine Electro-Mechanical Rotational Transformer (EMRT) arrangement for supplying electrical power to a rotating load while keeping the primary source stationary. It summarizes the architecture, declared simulation result, control comparison, energy-accounting rules, communication options, prototype prerequisites, and corpus position.

The work is a simulation brief and experimental plan, not a validated electromechanical product. No hardware run, independent efficiency measurement, fabrication authorization, or safety approval is claimed.

The academic manuscript supplies the full governed reference model, while the conceptual schematics provide the frame, power-path, control, and telemetry diagrams.

papers.title: EMRT Conceptual Schematics - Frames, Power Paths, Control, and Telemetry
papers.description_html:
This conceptual schematics companion explains the reference frames, power and reaction paths, local control loops, mechanical and optical telemetry concepts, and evidence boundary of a two-machine Electro-Mechanical Rotational Transformer (EMRT) arrangement.

The diagrams are explanatory system models rather than fabrication drawings. They do not specify certified component ratings, clearances, protection coordination, containment, construction details, or authorization to build or operate hardware.

The companion should be read with the academic manuscript and technical brief, which are published as separately citable EMRT works.
